newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds rebound, end up in thin market.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds rebound, end up in thin market.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bond prices shook off a weak opening to close modestly higher in lackluster holiday trade, dealers said.
The observance of Yom Kippur and the lack of major economic data ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting quashed trade, dealers said.
Investment-grade spreads held firm across the yield curve and high-yield securities remained mostly untraded except a few select issues.
"It's very quiet today because of the holiday. Nothing much has traded," one junk bond trader said.
Harrah's Jazz Co debt rose one to two points with the 14-1/4 percent first mortgage notes quoted at 54 bid, 57 offer at the close.
Ralph's Grocery 10.45 percent notes traded unchanged at a 99-3/4 bid, 100-1/4 offer. Ralph's 11.0 percent notes gained 1/8 of a point at a 99 bid, 100-1/8 offer.

Active media and telecommunication markets were unseen after sector paper popped up 1/2 to 1-1/4 points on Friday, traders said. Nextel Communications' zeros due 2003 traded up 1-1/2 points to 71-1/2 bid on Friday. Nextel's debt due 2004 traded up 3/4 at 62-1/2 bid.
In underlying markets, both Treasuries and U.S. equities roared back from severe deficits to close higher.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average reached a new unofficial high, rising 6.28 to 5894.74, after an early 53-point drop.

In the governments market, the benchmark 30-year bond erased early losses and closed up 8/32 at 96-19/32 to yield 7.02 percent after an unidentified Federal Reserve source reassured Wall Street that the Fed remains vigilant in its inflation fight.
